$comment: Schema for a LearningAssistant learning plan file. Each file represents one topic and organises content into a 3-level hierarchy: Module > Lesson > Concept.

topic_slug.description: Unique identifier for the topic. Lowercase, hyphen-separated. Must match the filename (topic-<slug>.json) and the corresponding files in questions/ and progress/.

description.example: An introduction to Kubernetes covering core objects, architecture, and common workflows.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when this plan was first created.

updated_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when this plan was last modified.

modules.description: Top-level groupings within the topic. Each module covers a broad area.

module_id.description: Unique identifier within this plan. Convention: M01, M02, …

description.example: The building blocks of a Kubernetes cluster: control plane, nodes, and networking.

lesson_id.description: Unique identifier within the module. Convention: M01-L01, M01-L02, …

description.example: The components that manage cluster state: kube-apiserver, etcd, kube-scheduler, and controller-manager.

concepts.description: The smallest teachable units. Each concept maps to one or more questions in the question bank.

concept_id.description: Unique identifier within the lesson. Convention: M01-L01-C01, …

description.description: A concise explanation of the concept — what it is and why it matters.
description.example: The kube-apiserver is the front-end for the Kubernetes control plane. It exposes the Kubernetes API and is the only component that interacts directly with etcd.

prerequisites.description: Optional list of concept_ids that should be understood before tackling this concept.

resources.description: Optional list of reference materials (links, book chapters, etc.).
